content:
Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president, CEO and board director, “effective immediately,” the chipmaker’s board announced Monday, noting the decision was made after consultation with “senior levels of the United States government.”

“The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA,” it said in a statement.

“In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” it went on.

The decision was reportedly made with guidance from President Donald Trump, who Semafor first reported dialed in to a board meeting to argue for his return. Trump later confirmed in a 50-minute phone interview with CNBC that he’d spoken “directly and indirectly” to the board to urge it to reinstate Huang.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” he told the outlet’s Eamon Javers. “And I convinced them.”

The president also said the board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” and that the U.S. gave “assurance at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.”

The board’s chair, Harvey C. Jones, said the move “is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.” Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news.

Huang resigned Nov. 12 after admitting to having an extramarital affair with a woman who was reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy. Last week, he released a public statement acknowledging he’d made “serious mistakes” but said he would be “honored” to return if asked.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he said in a post on X.

Video posted on social media on Monday appeared to show Nvidia employees greeting Huang with loud applause and chants of his name after his return.

“I’ve made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back,” he said, according to The New York Times.

“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said in one video shared by CNBC. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

The board said Monday that an investigation into Huang being “the target of a foreign intelligence effort” remains ongoing with Huang’s full support and cooperation and that his reinstatement, according to unidentified U.S. officials, “poses no national security risk.”

“I think the board acted really responsibly” in bringing Huang back into the company, Trump said, adding that the AI leader “did nothing wrong.”

“As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy,” he said.

Despite his return, Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter remain scheduled to testify on Capitol Hill early next month, a House Foreign Affairs Committee spokesperson told Punchbowl News, saying Huang’s return “changes nothing.”

Lawmakers are looking into Chinese-based companies’ ability to access advanced AI chips and whether the companies have been able to skirt U.S. export control laws.

“Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang is outrageous. We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), who serves on the House Intelligence Committee and is the top Democrat on the Select Committee on China, posted on X.

“Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him,” he continued.

Trump hailed Huang’s reinstatement in a Truth Social post Monday as beneficial to not just the company “but the American Economy.”

“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” he said, adding that the U.S. attorney general also said there is no evidence Huang engaged in any unlawful conduct.

“Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security,” he said.

Trump appeared to have had advanced knowledge of the announcement, having told a PBS News reporter earlier on Monday that Huang is “back where he should be.” He also said he called Huang after speaking with the board and “the deal was finished.”

“I called him up, and I said: ‘I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,’” he told CNBC.

Trump told reporters Friday that he’d discussed Huang with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and that Xi had called Huang a “brilliant man.” The president also said Monday that Xi might have asked Huang to lead a Chinese company if he wasn’t reinstated at Nvidia.
